docs.title: IndianConstitution
docs.text:
## *A Developer-First, Research-Grade Python Framework for the Constitution of India*

indianconstitution is a production-grade Python library providing programmatic, structured, and type-safe access to the complete text of the Constitution of India — including all 448 articles, 12 schedules, the Preamble, and amendments through the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023.

docs.title: Key Capabilities
docs.text:
• Typed Article API: Fully annotated Pydantic v2 data models (Article, Part, Schedule, SearchResult).
  • Inverted-Index Search: Sub-millisecond lexical search via built-in inverted index ($O(1)$ token lookup).
  • Graph Analysis: NetworkX-backed relational graph mapping inter-article cross-references.
  • Semantic / AI Search: Sentence-Transformers embeddings for contextual retrieval and RAG pipelines.
  • Multi-Format Export: Single-call export to JSON, CSV, and Markdown.
  • pandas Integration: Direct DataFrame generation for data science workflows.
  • Rich CLI: Terminal interface with syntax highlighting and interactive exploration.

docs.title: Quick Installation
docs.text:
# Core framework
pip install indianconstitution

# With data science integrations (pandas, NetworkX)
pip install "indianconstitution[data]"

# With AI & semantic search (sentence-transformers)
pip install "indianconstitution[ai]"

# Full installation
pip install "indianconstitution[data,ai]"

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
from indianconstitution import get_article, search, get_constitution

# Retrieve by article number
article = get_article("21A")
print(f"Article {article.number}: {article.title}")
# -> Article 21A: Right to Education

# Inverted-index search
results = search("equality before law", limit=5)
for r in results:
    print(f"[{r.number}] {r.title}")

# Graph analysis
ic = get_constitution()
related = ic.get_related_articles("32")
print("Articles referencing Article 32:", related["referenced_by"])

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: Complete documentation of the indianconstitution public API.

docs.title: get_constitution() -> Constitution
docs.text: Returns the global singleton instance of the Constitution engine.

docs.title: get_article(number: str) -> Optional[Article]
docs.text: Retrieves an Article object by number (e.g., '14', '21A'). Returns None if not found.

docs.title: search(query: str, limit: int = 10) -> List[Article]
docs.text: Performs inverted-index keyword search across all article titles and text.

docs.title: Constitution
docs.text:
class Constitution:
    def get_article(self, number: Union[int, str]) -> Optional[Article]: ...
    def search(self, query: str, limit: int = 10) -> List[Article]: ...
    def get_graph(self) -> networkx.DiGraph: ...
    def get_related_articles(self, number: str) -> Dict[str, List[str]]: ...
    def get_central_articles(self, limit: int = 10) -> List[Tuple[str, float]]: ...
    def semantic_search(self, query: str, top_k: int = 5) -> List[SearchResult]: ...
    def export(self, format: str, path: Union[str, Path]) -> None: ...
    def to_dataframe(self) -> pandas.DataFrame: ...

docs.title: Article
docs.text:
Pydantic v2 data model representing a single article.

  • number: str - Article number string (e.g., '21A')
  • title: str - Title of the article
  • content: str - Full text of the article
  • text: str - Property alias for content
  • part: Optional[int] - Inferred Part number (1–22)
  • chapter: Optional[int] - Chapter number within Part

docs.title: SearchResult
docs.text:
Inherits fields from Article and adds relevance score:

  • score: float - Similarity score (0.0 to 1.0)

docs.title: Command Line Interface (CLI)
docs.text: indianconstitution comes with a command-line interface powered by Typer and Rich.

docs.title: Commands Overview
docs.text: Command Usage Description get indianconstitution get <number> Retrieve and render a specific article search indianconstitution search <query> [--limit N] Full-text inverted index keyword search preamble indianconstitution preamble Render the Preamble with rich formatting related indianconstitution related <number> Show cross-references for an article stats indianconstitution stats Summary metrics (article count, word count) export indianconstitution export <format> <output> Export corpus to JSON, CSV, or Markdown

docs.title: Retrieve Article 21A
docs.text: indianconstitution get 21A

docs.title: Search Keywords
docs.text: indianconstitution search "freedom of speech" --limit 5

docs.title: View Related Articles
docs.text: indianconstitution related 32

docs.title: Export Dataset
docs.text:
indianconstitution export json output.json
indianconstitution export csv output.csv

docs.title: Code Examples
docs.text:
The repository includes executable examples under examples/:

  • basic_usage.py: Core retrieval and search.
  • graph_analysis.py: NetworkX graph cross-references.
  • pandas_export.py: DataFrame analytics.
  • rag_pipeline.py: Context building for LLMs.
  • semantic_search.py: Vector embedding search.
  • json_export.py: Multi-format data export.
  • cli_demo.py: Programmatic CLI usage.

Interactive Jupyter Notebooks are available in notebooks/: - notebooks/Introduction.ipynb - notebooks/AI_RAG.ipynb - notebooks/LegalResearch.ipynb - notebooks/SemanticSearch.ipynb

docs.title: What amendments are included?
docs.text: The corpus is updated and verified up to the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 (Women's Reservation Bill).

docs.title: Does this package require internet access?
docs.text: No. In core mode, indianconstitution operates 100% offline with zero external network calls.

docs.title: Is NetworkX required?
docs.text: No. NetworkX is optional. Core functions like get_article() and search() run without NetworkX. Graph features like get_graph() require pip install "indianconstitution[data]".

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide covers setup and fundamental concepts of the indianconstitution library.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python: 3.8, 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14
  • Dependencies: pydantic >= 2.0, typer >= 0.9, rich >= 13.0

docs.title: 1. Core Package
docs.text:
Minimal installation with zero external data-science heavy dependencies:

pip install indianconstitution

docs.title: 2. Data Science Extra
docs.text:
Includes pandas, networkx, and scipy for graph analysis and tabular workflows:

pip install "indianconstitution[data]"

docs.title: 3. AI / Semantic Search Extra
docs.text:
Includes sentence-transformers and torch for vector embeddings:

pip install "indianconstitution[ai]"

docs.title: Accessing Articles
docs.text:
from indianconstitution import get_article, get_constitution

# Fetch single article
art = get_article("14")
print(art.title)    # Equality before law
print(art.content)  # Full article text
print(art.part)     # 3 (Part III - Fundamental Rights)

# Access full Constitution instance
ic = get_constitution()
print(f"Total articles loaded: {len(ic)}")
print(f"Preamble: {ic.preamble[:150]}...")

docs.title: Multi-Format Data Export

docs.title: Keyword Search Engine
docs.text: indianconstitution includes a custom inverted-index search engine built directly into the core library without external dependencies.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Sub-millisecond Latency: $O(1)$ token lookup speed.
  • AND Logic: Multi-token queries return articles containing all query terms.
  • Zero Dependencies: Pure Python dictionary and set operations.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
from indianconstitution import search

# Single keyword
results = search("untouchability")

# Phrase / multi-token search
results = search("fundamental rights equality", limit=5)
for art in results:
    print(f"[{art.number}] {art.title}")

docs.title: Semantic & AI Search
docs.text: Semantic search empowers contextual retrieval beyond exact keyword matching, making it ideal for legal AI and RAG applications.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: pip install "indianconstitution[ai]"

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
from indianconstitution import get_constitution

ic = get_constitution()

# Natural-language query
results = ic.semantic_search(
    "protection against arbitrary state action",
    top_k=5
)

for r in results:
    print(f"Article {r.number}: {r.title} (score: {r.score:.4f})")

docs.title: RAG Integration Example
docs.text:
def build_rag_context(query: str) -> str:
    results = ic.semantic_search(query, top_k=3)
    return "\n---\n".join([f"**Article {r.number}**: {r.text}" for r in results])
